newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares seen up as Front elects new leader.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares seen up as Front elects new leader.

text.p: ** Bombay shares are likely to open higher as the United Front elects a new leader, ending a three-week political crisis that has rocked financial markets and paralysed government
** But news that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party is likely to support the government only from the outside will depress sentiment, traders say
** Prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral is due to face a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday at 0530 GMT
** Indian parties will later in the day set a timetable for the 1997/98 budget debate
** Shares of Reliance Industries seen in limelight ahead of financial results for 1996/97 (April-March) due on Tuesday
Bombay shares are likely to open sharply higher as the United Front elected a new leader, defusing a prolonged political crisis that has rocked financial markets, traders said.
But they said markets would be hit by the loss of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, whose Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) has quit the government but has said it will extend outside support.
"It's going to open up by around 50-100 points and then stop," said an equities salesman at a foreign brokerage.
"People are yet a little anxious about Chidambaram not being there," he said.
Indian prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral will face a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT).
Gujral, 77, was set to be sworn in as India's 12th prime minister on Monday at 10 a.m. (0430 GMT) at the head of a centre-left government supported by the Congress party.
Representatives of all political parties will meet Speaker P.A. Sangma later on Monday to decide when parliament will take up the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year that began on April 1.
"The only news that the market is looking for right now is that the TMC will change its mind and decide to be part of the government," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
"The main brain behind the budget was Chidambaram and if he's not there it could be a serious problem," he said.
The pro-business federal budget for 1997/98 announced on February 28 has yet to be approved by parliament.
Traders said financial results of largest private firm Reliance Industries would drive its share price higher. Results for 1996/97 (April-March) are due on Tuesday.
Reliance shares are expected to open sharply higher due to a higher bookclosure carryforward charge set over the weekend.
